subject: Isolated deployment decision heatmap & procurement path for MediCore
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen.park@medicore.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medicore.com
Date: 2026-08-15 09:12 -0700
Subject: Isolated deployment options for regulated inference workloads

Hi Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the intro last week. MediCore has an upcoming rollout (P1 pilot) that processes PHI and must be isolated from multi-tenant workloads. Key asks: encrypted-at-rest keys under our KMS, per-tenant audit logs, and a physically segregated GPU fleet (no shared racks).

We need a clear buy-vs-lease analysis and a recommendation: Redwood Private (on-prem VPC deployment) vs Redwood Dedicated (isolated tenant pool in our cloud). Our procurement team needs capex vs opex comparisons, lead times, and a minimum viable configuration to support the pilot (estimated 75 concurrent users, 2.2k tokens/sec peak, latency SLO 200ms p95).

Can you send a decision matrix + cost model and call out which path shortens time-to-live while preserving our compliance needs?

Thanks —
Helen
Helen Park
Head of AI Platforms, MediCore
helen.park@medicore.com

Subject: Re: Isolated deployment options for regulated inference workloads

Hi Helen —

Appreciate the clarity on constraints. Marissa and I will put together a heatmap showing tradeoffs across time-to-production, cost, data sovereignty, and operational burden. Initial questions we need to confirm before finalizing:

- Expected steady-state concurrent sessions for production (you mentioned 75 for the pilot; what is expected within 6 months?)
- Daily token throughput (approximate) and peak burst factor (x1.5, x2?)
- Any mandatory third-party audits beyond SOC 2 (e.g., HITRUST)?

Proposing a short call on Thursday 8/20 to walk the heatmap and procurement path — does 11:00 AM PT work? We'll include a baseline cost model and a 'min viable' rack SKU for Private.

Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18 08:30 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: MediCore sizing assumptions & comparisons (draft)

Team —

Draft assumptions for the heatmap and the cost model (please review):

- Workload: Llama-2-70B-like model, 16-token prompt avg, 120-token response avg.
- Pilot load: 75 concurrent sessions steady; growth to 250 concurrent within 6 months.
- SLO: 200ms p95; P50 goal 80ms.
- Data tenure: logs retained 7 years, audit exports monthly.

Sizing options considered:
- Private (on-prem / VPC private-control-plane): 4 racks (NVIDIA H100 equivalent) initially; scaled to 12 racks at steady-state. High capex, lead time 8–12 weeks for procurement and rack install. Lower per-token cost at scale, fully isolated.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity in our cloud): 2 node-pools sized for 75->250 concurrency with strict tenancy and physical isolation controls. Faster lead time (2–3 weeks), higher unit opex across time, simpler managed ops and patching.
- Hybrid: Staging on Dedicated, later conversion to Private once capacity commit justified.

Key cost model levers: GPU SKU choice, quantization profile, batching/latency tradeoffs, reserved term discounts. I attached the cost CSV + the decision heatmap.

Please add any missed constraints (regulatory, procurement thresholds, or preferred hardware vendors).

Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@medicore.com>, procurement@medicore.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19 09:20 -0700
Subject: MediCore: decision heatmap + recommended short/medium path (attachments)

Hi Helen —

Attached: medicore-decision-heatmap-20260819.xlsx and medicore-cost-model-v2.csv (links also included). TL;DR recommendation below.

Executive summary:
- Short path (pilot, required compliance controls, fastest time-to-live): Redwood Dedicated (reserved isolated pools). Lead time 2–3 weeks, Opex-first. Rationale: minimal infra turnaround, Redwood manages OS/patching and KMS integration, and we can provide per-tenant audit exports and dedicated racks in region.
- Medium/long path (steady-state cost at scale, maximum isolation): Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC / on-prem). Capex up-front, 8–12 week lead time, lower per-token cost beyond ~18 months for the projected growth curve. Better for customers requiring physical custody and direct KMS/HSM on their side.

Numbers (high level):
- Pilot (75 concurrency): Dedicated monthly opex estimate: $68k/mo (including reserved capacity uplift and 24/7 support).
- Private initial procurement: estimated one-time hardware + initial install ~ $1.85M (4-rack min), ongoing infra ops ~$35k/mo (network, power, security). Break-even: ~14–20 months depending on utilization and reserved discounts.

Recommended procurement path:
1) Start pilot on Redwood Dedicated (isolated tenant pool) to meet compliance and speed-to-market.
2) Execute a 12-month reserved capacity agreement with conversion credits toward Private hardware purchase if you decide to move.
3) Parallel: start procurement for Private hardware if MediCore prefers capex route — we'll provide a vendor-ready spec and install SOW.

Next steps: confirm concurrence on pilot sizing and whether procurement wants a vendor list and SOW. I set a follow-up for Thu 8/20 11:00 AM PT to walk the heatmap.

Attachments: medicore-decision-heatmap-20260819.xlsx (decision matrix), medicore-cost-model-v2.csv (detailed numbers), SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf (requested by your security team).

Karthik
